scene:
Three unlabelled areas read left to right, separated by generous space; do not number, title or name the areas.

LEFT AREA, the business's numbers: three horizontal bars stacked top to bottom and left-aligned, each clearly shorter than the one above: a long teal bar labelled REVENUE €20M; a medium teal bar labelled EBITDA €4M; a short ochre bar labelled NET PROFIT €1.5M.

MIDDLE AREA, what is being valued and how, top to bottom. At the top, a bridge equation drawn as three blocks in a row with a minus sign and an equals sign between them: a large teal block showing a small office building, labelled BUSINESS VALUE €60M; minus an ochre block showing a bank building, labelled NET DEBT €20M; equals a smaller teal block showing a stack of blank share certificates, labelled SHARES €40M. Below the equation, with clear space and NO arrows or lines connecting them to the equation, three magnifying glasses in a row, each looking at one object: a row of three small similar buildings, labelled MARKET COMPARISONS; a calendar with coins drifting in from the future along a curved arrow, labelled FUTURE CASH; a set of equipment and a server rack, labelled ASSETS.

RIGHT AREA, one assumption to challenge: a clipboard showing a stopwatch with a plain face and hands only (no digits) beside a single worker at a laptop configuring a customer's settings, labelled 80 HOURS PER SETUP. Below it three question tags stacked vertically, each with a small icon: a wrench labelled WHICH CHANGE?; a calendar labelled WHEN USABLE?; an open wallet labelled WHO FUNDS IT?

All coins are plain discs with no symbols; draw no dollar, euro or other currency signs on any object. Buildings, documents, screens, calendars and people carry no words, letters or numerals of their own. The minus and equals signs in the middle area are the only symbols besides the labels.

No chapter title, heading or book name anywhere; bars contain only their label, no coin or chart icons.

TEXT: draw exactly these labels, each once and nothing else: REVENUE €20M, EBITDA €4M, NET PROFIT €1.5M, BUSINESS VALUE €60M, NET DEBT €20M, SHARES €40M, MARKET COMPARISONS, FUTURE CASH, ASSETS, 80 HOURS PER SETUP, WHICH CHANGE?, WHEN USABLE?, WHO FUNDS IT? Any other text is a defect.
alt: Bars step down from €20 million of revenue to €4 million of EBITDA and €1.5 million of net profit; a bridge shows €60 million of business value minus €20 million of net debt equals €40 million for the shares, above three lenses for estimating value: market comparisons, future cash and assets; a clipboard shows 80 hours per customer setup and three questions: which change, when usable, who funds it.
caption: Read the numbers, separate the business from its shares, know how the estimate was made, and challenge the assumption that lands on your team.
